key_insight: A simple NLP- and claims-based phenotyping approach can identify anaphylaxis with strong performance, especially when using silver labels derived from clinical text and diagnosis codes.
clinical_relevance: This could help health systems find more anaphylaxis cases for research and quality improvement without relying on labor-intensive manual chart review.
method: Extracted features from clinical text using automated NLP.
Built weakly supervised phenotyping models using four NLP- and diagnosis code-based silver labels.
Evaluated performance against gold-standard abstracted outcomes in two health systems (KPWA and VUMC).
evidence_signal: The best model reached an AUC of 0.931 at KPWA, with PPV 0.52–0.77 and sensitivity 0.78–1.00 depending on site and threshold.
watch_item: Performance varied by site, suggesting the model may not transfer equally well where clinical text structure and availability differ.
paper_title: Identifying anaphylaxis using weakly-supervised prediction models and natural language processing
